chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated, saying: Some of our companions narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Abu Wahb, from Muhammad ibn Mansur, who said: I asked a virtuous servant (of Allah), peace be upon him,

about the saying of Allah: 'Say: My Lord has only prohibited indecencies, those of them that are apparent as well as those that are concealed, and the sin, and the transgression without right, and that you associate with Allah that for which He has sent down no authority, and that you say about Allah what you do not know.' (He) said, so he said: Indeed, the Qur'an has an apparent meaning and a hidden meaning,

so all that which Allah has prohibited in the Qur'an is impermissible in its apparent sense as it is in the apparent sense, and the hidden aspect of that is the Imams of Injustice. And all that which Allah the Exalted has permitted in the Book is permissible and it is the apparent, and the hidden aspect of that is the Imams of Truth.
ai.seo_question: What is the hidden meaning of Allah's prohibitions and permissions in the Qur'an according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Numani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, the scholar highlights the Shia hermeneutical principle that divine rulings possess both an exoteric (zahir) and esoteric (batin) dimension. While the literal prohibitions apply to all, the 'Imams of Injustice' represent the hidden corruption of divine law, whereas the 'Imams of Truth' embody the true, living interpretation of what is permissible, thereby establishing the Imams as the ultimate authorities in distinguishing truth from falsehood.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (11) Muhammad bin Ya’qoob narrated from some of his companions from Ahmad bin Muhammad from al-Husayn bin Sa’eed from Abu Wahab that Muhammad bin Mansoor had said: “I have asked a virtuous slave (of Allah), peace be upon him,

about the saying of Allah, “My Lord has only prohibited indecencies, those of them that are apparent as well as those that are concealed,” and he said: “The Qur’an has apparent meanings and hidden meanings.

All of those that Allah has prohibited in the Qur’an are impermissible as they have been mentioned apparently whereas the hidden thing in that is the imams of injustice and all of those that Allah has permitted are permissible as they are apparent whereas the hidden thing among them is the imams of guidance.”
